jurisdiction.name: Kenya
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Kenya governs AI through its Kenya Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2025-2030 and through binding rules on automated decisions in the Data Protection Act 2019 and the Data Protection (General) Regulations 2021, which require human intervention, bias safeguards and impact assessments for algorithmic decisions. In 2026 the Pharmacy and Poisons Board set rules for AI-enabled medical device software, and the Kenya Bureau of Standards has a national code of practice for AI applications (KS 3007:2025). A draft national AI and emerging technologies policy, Data Protection Commissioner and Central Bank AI guidance notes, and a Senate Artificial Intelligence Bill 2026 are all still pending.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy
Office of the Data Protection Commissioner
narrative.review_notes: This review was first completed on 12 October 2026 and redone in a longer pass on 13 October 2026, covering Parliament, the ICT ministry, each line ministry and each sector regulator. The final AI strategy, the 2025 draft strategy and the 2026 draft AI policy were read in full. Not yet verified from the official text: material on the national law reports site and the ICT Authority's site. The KEBS AI code of practice is a paid standard and is recorded as located only. The Senate AI Bill 2026 and several undated or draft documents are tracked as leads.

instruments.summary: Draft national policy (cover: 'Kenya Artificial Intelligence and Other Emerging Technologies Policy, July 2026') setting a cross-sector framework for the governance, development, deployment and use of AI and other emerging technologies, building on the AI Strategy 2025-2030, the Digital Master Plan and the Data Protection Act. It adopts a risk-based, full-lifecycle approach with stronger assessment, documentation and oversight duties for high-risk systems, applies to public and private actors in Kenya, foreign providers whose AI outputs are used in Kenya and all public-sector AI procurement, and proposes an AI and other Emerging Technologies Council for strategic oversight. Sector regulators would issue aligned sectoral guidelines and standards, and new legislation is proposed to formalise the framework.

instruments.summary: Kenya's first national AI strategy, covering 2025-2030, aiming to make Kenya Africa's leading AI hub for model innovation, research and commercialisation while safeguarding data sovereignty, cybersecurity and ethical oversight. It rests on three pillars (AI digital infrastructure; data; AI research, innovation and commercialisation) supported by enablers on talent, governance, investment, and ethics, equity and inclusion, with priority sectors including agriculture, security, health, education and public services. It sets a phased implementation starting with policy, infrastructure and capacity building, followed by a national AI policy, research hubs, pilots and a monitoring and evaluation framework.

instruments.publisher_name: Office of the Data Protection Commissioner
instruments.current_status: In force since 25 November 2019 (Act No. 24 of 2019, Kenya Gazette Supplement No. 181, 11 November 2019; assented 8 November 2019). It is now cited as Cap. 411C in the revised laws.
instruments.summary: Kenya's general data protection law, establishing the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner and regulating the processing of personal data. Section 35 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal or similarly significant effects, unless necessary for a contract, authorised by law with safeguards, or based on consent; controllers must notify the data subject and, on request, reconsider the decision or take a new one not based solely on automated processing. Section 31 requires a data protection impact assessment for high-risk processing.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding rules on automated decision-making and profiling that apply to AI systems processing personal data.

instruments.english_title: Data Protection (General) Regulations, 2021 (Legal Notice No. 263 of 2021)
instruments.issuing_authority: Cabinet Secretary for Information, Communication, Technology, Innovation and Youth Affairs (under section 71 of the Data Protection Act, 2019)
instruments.publisher_name: Office of the Data Protection Commissioner
instruments.current_status: Made on 7 December 2021 and published as Legal Notice No. 263 in Kenya Gazette Supplement No. 236 of 31 December 2021. No separate commencement date stated in the text read.
instruments.summary: Implementing regulations under the Data Protection Act, 2019. Regulation 22 requires controllers and processors using solely automated individual decision-making to inform data subjects, give meaningful information about the logic involved, explain significance and consequences, prevent errors, use appropriate mathematical or statistical procedures, process data so as to eliminate discriminatory effects and bias, and ensure human intervention is available. Regulation 49 lists automated decision-making with legal or similar effects, including profiling or algorithmic means, among the high-risk processing that requires a data protection impact assessment.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Kenya's most detailed binding rules on algorithmic decision-making: explainability, bias and human-intervention duties plus mandatory DPIA.

instruments.official_title: Draft Guidance Note on Artificial Intelligence in the Banking Sector
instruments.english_title: Draft Guidance Note on Artificial Intelligence in the Banking Sector
instruments.current_status: Draft (cover dated August 2026) published for public comment on 10 September 2026 with other draft prudential guidelines and guidance notes; comments due by 7 November 2026. To be issued under s.57(1) CBK Act, s.33(4) Banking Act and s.48(2A) Microfinance Act once final.
instruments.summary: Draft CBK guidance applying to banks, microfinance banks, credit reference bureaus, money remittance providers, non-deposit-taking credit providers and non-operating holding companies that develop, use or rely on third-party AI. It sets board and senior-management responsibilities, ethical principles (fairness, transparency and explainability, privacy), an AI risk-management and model-risk life cycle, rules for generative and agentic AI, consumer disclosure and human review for critical decisions, and requires institutions to seek CBK approval before deploying AI. Institutions would file an annual AI register and report material AI incidents within 24 hours and quarterly.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First AI-specific supervisory instrument from a Kenyan financial regulator; proposes prior approval, registers and incident reporting.

instruments.summary: ODPC guidance on how the Data Protection Act and its regulations apply to public and private entities that develop, deploy or procure AI systems processing personal data in Kenya. It applies the data protection principles, lawful bases and data-subject rights (including the section 35 right not to be subject to solely automated decisions) across a seven-stage AI lifecycle, and bars using personal data scraped from the internet as training data without a lawfulness assessment. It lists high-risk AI applications (e.g. credit scoring, health diagnostics, biometric recognition, employment screening) that require a DPIA, DPO involvement, meaningful human review and regular algorithmic audits, adds generative-AI duties, and includes a compliance checklist.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First AI-specific guidance from Kenya's data protection regulator; sets high-risk categories and lifecycle duties.

instruments.english_title: Guideline on Regulation of Medical Device Software in Kenya (MDSW), HPT/PER/GUD/099 Rev. 0
instruments.issuing_authority: Pharmacy and Poisons Board (Ministry of Health)
instruments.current_status: Published by the Pharmacy and Poisons Board as document HPT/PER/GUD/099, Revision 0, dated February 2026 on its cover; available on the PPB downloads page.
instruments.summary: PPB guideline on the registration and regulation of software as a medical device and software in a medical device in Kenya, covering essential safety and performance principles, labelling, versioning, verification and validation, clinical evidence and cybersecurity. Section 2.8 sets requirements for AI-enabled medical devices: it adopts the ten Good Machine Learning Practice principles, requires AI device design, training, validation, retraining and deployment to run under an ISO 13485 quality management system, and specifies data (e.g. datasets) to submit for registration. It also requires ethical issues such as bias in AI, patient consent and data protection to be addressed.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First AI-specific requirements from Kenya's health products regulator, covering AI-enabled medical devices.

leads.note: Official document on ict.go.ke (https://ict.go.ke/node/897; PDF https://ict.go.ke/sites/default/files/2025-12/Kenya%20National%20AI%20Strategy%202025-2030%20Implementation%20Roadmap.pdf), read in full; no stated publication date and no issuer statement in the text (only a CMS posting date). Sets infrastructure, data governance, national LLM, public-sector AI and governance actions to 2030. Promote if a dated version or launch notice appears.

leads.title: Government Digital Enterprise Architecture (GEA) Framework - Government Enterprise Architecture Guidelines, 1st Edition (ICTA GEA: 001:2025)
leads.english_title: Government Digital Enterprise Architecture Framework (draft for public participation)
leads.issuing_authority: ICT Authority (published for comment by the Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy)
leads.note: Draft posted on ict.go.ke 'Call for Public Participation' (https://ict.go.ke/sites/default/files/2026-09/Government%20Enterprise%20Architecture%20%28GEA%29_0.pdf); consultant report dated 30 March 2026; contains a chapter 'Aligning GEA strategy with AI' and a GEA/AI alignment guide for ministries, counties, departments and agencies. No closing date or adoption notice; AI is one chapter of a general EA framework. Promote if adopted and the AI chapter is retained.

leads.title: KS ISO/IEC 42001:2023 Information technology - Artificial intelligence - Management system
leads.english_title: Kenyan adoption of ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management system)
leads.note: Listed on the KEBS webstore (https://webstore.kebs.org/index.php?route=product/product&product_id=19744) with other AI adoptions (KS ISO/IEC TR 24028:2020, KS ISO/IEC 24030:2024, data life cycle framework, bias in AI systems, neural-network robustness, SQuaRE for AI). No national adoption date stated (designation carries the ISO edition year); Kenya Gazette declaration not checked (Kenya Law unreachable). Promote once the gazette notice declaring the standard is found.

leads.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Policy for the Judiciary of Kenya
leads.english_title: Artificial Intelligence Policy for the Judiciary of Kenya (draft)
leads.note: Judiciary announced an AI Adoption Policy Framework on judiciary.go.ke (news item, August 2025); a draft policy and draft practice directions on AI use in court filings circulate only on third-party sites. No official text found on judiciary.go.ke; Kenya Law (gazette, practice directions) unreachable. Promote when published officially.

leads.title: Media Handbook for Reporting on Artificial Intelligence in Kenya
leads.english_title: Media Handbook for Reporting on Artificial Intelligence in Kenya
leads.note: Official document on mediacouncil.or.ke (https://mediacouncil.or.ke/sites/default/files/downloads/MEDIA%20HANDBOOK%20FOR%20REPORTING%20ON%20ARTIFICIAL%20INTELLIGENCE%20IN%20KENYA.pdf); no stated publication date. MCK public notice put this and a 'Media Guide on the Use of Artificial Intelligence in Kenya' out for comment until 26 January 2025; final status and the AI use guide itself not found.

leads.title: Guidelines for Election Coverage 2027
leads.english_title: Media Council of Kenya Guidelines for Election Coverage 2027 (chapter on AI and emerging technologies)
leads.note: Official document on mediacouncil.or.ke (https://mediacouncil.or.ke/sites/default/files/downloads/Guidelines%20for%20Election%20Coverage%202027_0.pdf) with a chapter on AI and emerging technologies (deepfakes, synthetic media, human oversight of AI content); no stated publication date.

leads.title: Communications Authority of Kenya Emerging Technologies Regulatory Sandbox
leads.english_title: Communications Authority of Kenya regulatory sandbox (covers AI-driven services)
leads.note: Official page https://www.ca.go.ke/regulatory-sandbox lists AI-driven services among testable categories; no framework document, guideline or date on the page. Promote if the sandbox framework/guidelines are published.

leads.title: Survey on Artificial Intelligence in the Banking Sector
leads.english_title: CBK Survey on Artificial Intelligence in the Banking Sector
leads.note: Official document on centralbank.go.ke (https://www.centralbank.go.ke/uploads/banking_sector_reports/595566510_Survey%20on%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20in%20the%20Banking%20Sector.pdf); survey issued March 2025, report has no stated publication date (only a CMS post date). Assessment of AI adoption and risks used to inform the 2026 draft AI guidance note.

leads.title: Guidance Note on Emerging Technologies
leads.english_title: ODPC Guidance Note on Emerging Technologies (July 2026)
leads.issuing_authority: Office of the Data Protection Commissioner
leads.note: Hosted on odpc.go.ke (https://www.odpc.go.ke/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Emerging-Tech-Guidance-Note.-July-2026.pdf); covers IoT, cloud, blockchain, biometrics; mentions AI only in passing and refers to the AI guidance note. Out of scope as a record.

leads.title: Ministry of Education AI in Education Guidelines (in development)
leads.note: Reported in development with UNICEF (co-creation workshop August 2026); no official document found on education.go.ke.
